text:
Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing how it works on the outside. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to read. For example, you might break a long, complicated function into smaller, simpler ones, or you might give variables clearer names. This does not add new features or fix bugs; it only improves the design.

One important reason to refactor is to reduce "technical debt." When you write code quickly, it can become messy and hard to understand later, like a pile of unpaid interest. By refactoring regularly, you keep this debt low, which makes future changes faster and less risky. In the long run, a small investment in refactoring saves a lot of time and stress.
